messages:
kevin: Heads up — noticed quota attribution noise in staging after the policy header rename. Console shows ~30% of requests unattributed. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: Saw the same in dev. Quick debug: TS SDK normalizes header casing, python/go clients don't by default. Might be a casing + rename mismatch.

maria: Integration tests against internal-proxy are intermittently 400ing when header comes in as `x-route-policy` vs `X-Route-Policy`. Policy router added stricter checks in v2.

olivia: Correct — policy-router v2 emits `X-Redwood-Route` (new canonical name) and also tightened header validation to avoid smuggling. We didn't expect older SDKs to refuse the alternate casing.

jen: Oof. We should avoid breaking client libraries. Options: 1) add a canonicalization shim in the proxy 2) add fallbacks in SDKs 3) revert the header rename. Thoughts?

kevin: Reverting is painful for rollout semantics. Prefer proxy shim + SDK fallback to be safe, then flip the canonical name once SDKs are patched.

sam: TS already has an accept-both behavior. I can cut a Python patch this week to check both `X-Redwood-Route` and lowercased `x-redwood-route`. Go's stdlib canonicalizes header keys which makes it awkward — rafael likely needs to add explicit checks in transport.

maria: Quick concern for Console telemetry: we rely on the header key to tag routes. If the proxy shims keys, will telemetry still attribute correctly?

olivia: Proxy shim plan: we will normalize keys internally and proxy both variants upstream so existing services/telemetry continue to see the key they expect. Telemetry will read the canonical value we set in the proxy trace metadata.

jen: Proposed rollout plan (prelim):
- canary proxy shim in region A for 48h (monitor for 4x regression)
- ship Python + Go SDK minor release with fallback header mapping
- expand shim to all regions and monitor console quota attribution dashboards
- finalize header rename and remove shims after 2w stable

kevin: Owners: olivia -> proxy shim, sam -> python + coord with ts, rafael -> go client patch, maria -> console dashboard monitor. I'll open the infra ticket and a follow-up tracking board.

sam: Quick test snippets for SDKs/infra:```
# curl tests
curl -H "X-Redwood-Route: project-A" https://internal-proxy.staging/redwood
curl -H "x-redwood-route: project-A" https://internal-proxy.staging/redwood
```
Python fallback example:```
headers = {"X-Redwood-Route": route}
# fallback for older callers
if "x-redwood-route" in incoming:
    headers["X-Redwood-Route"] = incoming["x-redwood-route"]
```

rafael: I'll prototype Go transport changes today. Likely add explicit header lookup using http.Header.Get("X-Redwood-Route") and also check strings.ToLower for legacy keys. Should be a tiny patch.

maria: I'll add a console tile that highlights untagged requests and a quick alert (pager disabled, slack notify) for attribution >5% in 1h window.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: infra/canary/proxy-shim -> queued (ETA ~2h) :hourglass: 

jen: If we stick to this plan we should avoid a wide break. Can we set a hard cutoff date for finalizing the rename?

kevin: Let's aim for 2 weeks from shim canary start, contingent on <1% untagged after SDK releases. I'll create the RFC with timelines. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll open the python PR and link it here when ready.

rafael: Go PR incoming in a few hours.

maria: I'll create the console dashboard PR and test cases.

kevin: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for coordination. I'll paste infra ticket + RFC here once created.
